FY2026: CEO 'We continue to believe our 2026 revenue will be around $1.1 billion this year'; CFO: 'this revenue level is limited by our production capacity and supply chain, not market demand, which we believe is much larger.'

items.signal_prefix: 1.6T RAMP BEGINS: full qualification of AOI's first 1.6T

set.signal: 1.6T RAMP BEGINS: CFO: 'We expect full qualification of our first 1.6Tb product by this customer within the next couple of weeks, followed by shipments of 1.6Tb beginning later this quarter' - the long-term major hyperscale customer that placed AOI's first 1.6T volume order in Q1; CEO: 'I think AOI will be the fourth supplier qualified by one big hyperscale data center customer for 1.6T transceiver.' CFO: 'We continue to expect that shipments of these orders will return this customer as a 10% plus customer for us in Q3.' CEO: 'right now we have more than $200 million orders in hand. I would say right now our target is to finish all the orders by sometime in Q2.' CFO on that order: 'we'll start deliveries on that probably very late in the third quarter and then ramp into the fourth quarter. I think the bulk of it should get delivered in the fourth quarter, and then there may be a tail into the first quarter', calling it 'just the very beginning' of what AOI expects to be significant 1.6T orders from this customer. Q4 1.6T (CEO): 'we still believe we can deliver more than, I would say, $70 million of revenue in Q4 for 1.6T transceiver'; 'what we can commit, maybe, I would say $70 million-$80 million in Q4. Not because of capacity, because, I would say, material constraint'; for Q1 2027 1.6T revenue, 'Q1 next year will be double Q4 or more than double' - 'That's our target right now.' The CFO confirmed an analyst's estimate of about $330M of combined 800G and 1.6T revenue in Q4 as 'about right, directionally'. Longer term (CEO): 'I think overall, based on the customer feedback, the volume we're talking about is more than 500,000 transceivers per month by end of next year', worth 'I would say $300 million-$350 million' per month.
set.figure: >$200M 1.6T orders in hand; Q4 1.6T >$70M (commit maybe $70-80M); Q4 800G+1.6T ~$330M (CFO: 'about right, directionally'); >500k units/mo ($300-350M/mo) by end of next year per customer feedback

items.reason: The ~$330M Q4 figure was the analyst's arithmetic, confirmed only 'directionally' by the CFO (now attributed); 'now sized at' implied a change the call does not state; hedges lost on the 10%-customer return ('continue to expect'), the delivery timing ('probably', 'I think the bulk'), the Q4 commitment ('maybe') and the 500k/month volume ('I think ... based on the customer feedback').
items.evidence: Actually, we'll start deliveries on that probably very late in the third quarter and then ramp into the fourth quarter. I think the bulk of it should get delivered in the fourth quarter

set.signal: CPO / ELSFP EXTERNAL LASER SOURCE ECONOMICS: ELSFP (external light source for co-packaged optics) is in very limited production now; CFO: 'we anticipate ramping production later this year and into 2027, ultimately culminating in about 400,000 pieces per month in 2028.' Laser power scaling (CEO): the CPO laser is a 300mW laser vs 70mW in the 800G transceiver and 100mW in the 1.6T transceiver, and 'The size is about six times or even higher'; 'I think the next generation of EOSAP will be using DWDM', where 'I think the yield loss will be easily 40%-50% compared to 1310 wavelengths', so to meet CPO demand the market 'needs to be 8 to 10 times bigger compared to today'; laser equipment ordered today takes 'minimum 21 months to 24 months to start manufacturing high volume'. Customers (CEO): 'Right now, we already have about five customers. They all come with some kind of very aggressive demand for the next three, four years'; 'for certain pin, CPO laser and ESP, several customer have qualified AOI', and DWDM is where customers focus. High-volume manufacturing: 'I would say more like the late Q3 next year.' Houston laser fab: 'the overall capacity will increase by almost 300% by Q3 next year', plus a clean room for a second fab in the Houston area about four times the size of the current facility (adding MOCVD, epi, steppers). Margin mix (CEO): 'gross margin for laser is about 55%-65%. For EOSAP, the gross margin should be more than 50%, that's more like Q3, Q4 next year.' CFO: 'We just can't make enough of them to be involved in their current first-generation deployments because there's just not enough capacity' - lasers for AOI's own transceivers come first.

items.label: Applied Optoelectronics Q2 FY2026 (08-06-2026)
items.signal_prefix: BOTTLENECK HAS MOVED FROM LASERS TO DSP/TIA

set.signal: AOI'S BIG CHALLENGE IS DSP/TIA, NOT LASERS. CEO: 'Right now, the big challenge, as I say, is the DSP and TIA' for 800G or 1.6T transceivers; 'Especially 1.6T, I think the whole supply chain is very tight. Good news is I think the supplier put AOI as the fourth priority, and it's a long-term partnership', with discussions with the key suppliers 'almost every week or twice a week'. Competitors' 'number one issue is not the DSP, it's this, and we don't have this problem, okay? AOI making our own laser'; the CEO also said 'laser is the biggest bottleneck right now for the transceiver business'. CFO: in-house laser manufacturing 'has allowed us to avoid some of the shortages that have affected others in the industry.' INDIUM PHOSPHIDE SUBSTRATE (CFO): 'we've secured supply out into next year. We're not currently limited by substrate capacity', and the situation is 'incrementally better than it was last earnings call'; CEO: 'we have enough inventory, we have enough supply until end of next year'. AOI 'just move into a four-inch substrate volume manufacture', already has two substrate suppliers in Europe, two in Japan and three in China, and is 'very aggressive to have some kind of partnership with two, three supplier. Even maybe the possible, I would say, potential joint venture', looking to the volume needed in 2028 and 2029, as AOI's laser capacity increase is 'much, much more than a factor of 10'. Equipment (CFO): 'our reliance on proprietary in-house developed machinery heavily insulates us from the broader equipment supply bottlenecks in the industry. There are exceptions to this, of course'.
set.figure: DSP/TIA = AOI's big challenge (CEO: supplier puts AOI as 'fourth priority'); InP substrate supply until end of next year; 4-inch substrate volume production

items.reason: 'Bottleneck has moved' was editorial (the CEO described AOI's own constraint vs competitors'); 'negotiating' a JV overstated 'very aggressive to have some kind of partnership ... potential joint venture'; hedges ('I think') and the CFO's 'exceptions' caveat restored.
items.evidence: Right now, the big challenge, as I say, is the DSP and TIA. Okay? For 800G or 1.6T transceiver.
